newsitem.title: FRANCE: AGF weakens as bid speculation fades.
newsitem.headline: AGF weakens as bid speculation fades.

text.p: Shares in French insurer AGF were down 2.38 percent at 1417 GMT after German insurer Allianz said it was looking at French state-controlled insurer GAN as a possible bid target.
"Allianz has said they are interested in GAN so the bid speculation that was in AGF has shifted to GAN," said one analyst.

AGF shares, which have been powered higher by speculation that Allianz was interested in the insurer, were off five francs at 205.50 francs while GAN shares were up 0.75 percent or one franc at 134.60.
Dominique Bazy, head of the French arm of Allianz, said on Wednesday that the insurer was looking at money-losing GAN as a possible acquisition.

"Gan Assurances is clearly an opportunity, we will look at it. But we don't want to grow for the sake of growing but to make profits," he told a news conference on Wednesday at which Allianz France announced a profit of 145 million francs following a loss of 335 million the previous year.
At the same meeting, however, Roberto Gavazzi, Allianz board member in charge of western European operations, said, "I never said that we were not interested" in AGF.
Allianz told reporters it wanted to increase its presence in France.
Gavazzi said Allianz "is not satisfied with its situation in France and remains open to all solutions. Right now, Allianz is not carrying out any operations. There is no urgency."
